knowledge_point.title: Computing a Tangent or Cotangent Using the Pythagorean Identity

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110758/assets/05b15f99ee3f8c1297d6013f00c621dc317540402c6d9b1479f64c1bceb484e9.png)

The diagram above shows the unit circle. Given that the $y$-coordinate of the point $P$ is $\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5},$ use the Pythagorean identity to find $tan⁡\theta .$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186110758/assets/18719bf6608fbb626c8eef093e5a9bd4cacaeca71eed77c631d9f2696cd21107.png)

Any point $(x,y)$ on the unit circle is related to the central angle $\theta $ as follows:

$$
x=cos⁡\theta ,\,y=sin⁡\theta 
$$

We're given that $y=\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5}$ at the point $P.$ Therefore, we have

$$
sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5}.
$$

We can use the Pythagorean identity to find $cos⁡\theta :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1 \\ {cos}^{2}⁡\theta  & =1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta  \\ cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $sin⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}cos⁡\theta  & =\pm \sqrt{1-{(\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5})}^{2}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{1-\frac{18}{25}} \\  & =\pm \sqrt{\frac{7}{25}} \\  & =\pm \frac{\sqrt{7}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We select the positive answer since $cos⁡\theta $ is positive in the first quadrant. So, $cos⁡\theta =\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5}.$

Knowing that $tan⁡\theta =\frac{sin⁡\theta }{cos⁡\theta },$ we have

$$
tan⁡\theta =\frac{(\frac{\sqrt{18}}{5})}{(\frac{\sqrt{7}}{5})}=\frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{7}}.
$$

Finally, we rationalize the denominator.

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\theta  & =\frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{7}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{18}}{\sqrt{7}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{18\cdot 7}}{7} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{126}}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
